watermelon.general_guidance: Watermelons favor well-drained sandy soils and warm weather. Most Florida acreage is planted in late winter for May-June harvest, ahead of other states. cotton.general_guidance: Cotton is a North Florida crop planted from late April into early June once soils are warm. Most Florida soils have a compacted layer, so subsoiling or strip tillage helps roots. Plant seed shallow (1/2 to 1 inch), rotate with peanuts or grasses to manage nematodes, and use growth regulators to control plant height on fertile ground.

field_corn.general_guidance: Field corn is planted in early spring in North and Central Florida; waiting until after March 1 reduces freeze risk. peanut.general_guidance: Peanuts do best on well-drained sandy or loamy sand soils in North Florida. Rotate with grasses such as bahiagrass or corn to limit diseases and nematodes, and avoid planting peanuts in the same field more than one year in three. Peanuts need calcium in the pegging zone, so soil-test and apply gypsum when calcium is low. Inoculate seed with rhizobia in fields without a recent peanut history.

potato.general_guidance: Florida potatoes are a winter-spring crop, centered on the Hastings area in the northeast and on South Florida farms. A slightly acidic soil helps limit common scab.

snap_bean.general_guidance: Snap beans are a short-season crop (about 55-65 days) grown in fall, winter and spring, including on South Florida muck. sweet_corn.general_guidance: Florida sweet corn is grown from fall through spring, with large acreage on the muck soils near Belle Glade and on sandy soils elsewhere. cabbage.general_guidance: Cabbage is a cool-season crop planted in fall and winter, with major acreage around Hastings in Northeast Florida. sugarcane.general_guidance: Florida sugarcane is concentrated on the organic muck soils south of Lake Okeechobee, with some acreage on nearby sands. It is a multi-year crop: one planting is usually harvested for several seasons. Growers manage the water table to supply water and slow muck subsidence, and fertilizer needs on muck differ from sandy soils, so follow soil tests. A sugar mill within hauling distance is essential.
